name: Benign Cephalic Histiocytosis
aliases: Benign Cephalic Histiocytosis of the Infant

criteria.description: Presence of multiple asymptomatic, small, yellow to red-brown papules primarily on the head and neck in infants or young children
Skin biopsy showing dermal infiltration by non-Langerhans cell histiocytes without Birbeck granules
Histiocytes positive for CD68 and negative for CD1a and S100 protein
No evidence of systemic disease or organ involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical clinical presentation with confirmatory histopathology and immunohistochemistry findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; spontaneous resolution is typical.

laboratory: Normal blood counts and inflammatory markers
imaging: Not typically required; no characteristic imaging findings
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating dermal infiltration by non-Langerhans histiocytes
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68, negative for CD1a and S100

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of Birbeck granules on electron microscopy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive or ulcerating skin lesions
Systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or organomegaly
Lesions persisting beyond early childhood without resolution
references: Harms PW, et al. Benign Cephalic Histiocytosis: Clinicopathologic Study of 12 Cases. Am J Dermatopathol. 2016.
Weitzman S, Jaffe R. Uncommon Histiocytic Disorders: The Non-Langerhans Cell Histiocytoses. Pediatr Blood Cancer. 2005.
